name: Czech
modelReview: built 2026-11-13 by Claude Fable 5.2 from usage notes written in Czech with no knowledge of cron, a rule book derived from them, the lexicon and the visible paradigms, after two schedule reads and five blind fluency reads of the rows and seven author passes; the renderer was built by an agent that saw no other renderer and no held-out row: 153 of 153 held-out rows passed on the first judged run. One hard-case row contradicted its rule and was corrected (four years are a list). The forms of the last author pass, about thirty places where the rule book was silent and the builder chose a general rule, and the built output beyond the rows have had no independent read; no blind recovery has been run. After the build one stutter was found and repaired test-first («vždy 1. dne v měsíci vždy 20 minut po…»), and rows were added for the code no row had reached; a sweep of 19,000 patterns in the family that broke Italian (two cadences together in one field) found no wrong schedule. Minutes, seconds, hours at one minute and days of the month that are runs and cadences together (more than seven values, at most three parts) are said as their parts (2026-11-13, no independent read yet). Held to the length gate the same day: a cadence of five hours or more beside several minutes is said as a cadence, and more than six clock times no longer each become a window of seconds (205 over-budget shapes to none)), and the Quartz `W` day is said «o víkendu místo toho …», the wording the maintainer chose over the spelled-out condition; Czech passes the length gate on both measures. None of these forms has had an independent fluency read. The maintainer, a native speaker, ruled that the short style's capitalised table forms («Po až Pá») are normal; 2026-11-13: says when both day fields must match (a day field written from a star beside a restricted one, as in Vixie cron), in rows, rule and renderer written by Claude Sonnet 5.5 from this rule book's seed and reviewed by Claude Fable 5.2; a blind Sonnet reader told these sentences from the union's 16 times of 16, and none has had a blind fluency read
